title: Manu Bhaker and Tajinderpal Singh Toor to Carry India's Flag at Asian Games
excerpt: Double Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker and two-time Asian Games shot put champion Tajinderpal Singh Toor will lead the Indian contingent into the Paloma Mizuho Stadium on September 19 as India aims to surpass its record Hangzhou medal haul.
body:
• Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker and two-time Asian Games shot put champion Tajinderpal Singh Toor will carry India's flag at the opening ceremony on September 19.
  • Bhaker's selection was confirmed by Chef de Mission Sahdev Yadav; the Athletics Federation of India confirmed Toor as the second flag-bearer.
  • The ceremony takes place at the Paloma Mizuho Stadium in Nagoya from 2:30 PM to 4:30 PM IST, opening the 20th Asian Games.
  • India fields a 500-plus athlete contingent aiming to surpass its record 107-medal haul from Hangzhou 2023.

Two champions, one flag

Manu Bhaker and Tajinderpal Singh Toor will carry the Indian tricolour at the opening ceremony of the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya on Saturday, September 19. India's Chef de Mission Sahdev Yadav confirmed Bhaker's selection on Friday, telling reporters, "Manu Bhaker will be one of the flag-bearers." The Athletics Federation of India later announced Toor as the second flag-bearer, pairing an Olympic medallist with one of the country's most decorated Asian Games champions.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=p8u-0KI3Qhc

The ceremony is scheduled at the Paloma Mizuho Stadium in Nagoya — officially the Nagoya City Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium — from 2:30 PM to 4:30 PM Indian Standard Time, marking the formal start of the 20th Asian Games. The Games run from September 19 to October 4, with athletes from 45 countries and regions competing across 43 sports and 469 medal events. Japan is hosting the Asian Games for the third time, after Tokyo in 1958 and Hiroshima in 1994.

Bhaker's landmark record

Bhaker, 24, arrives in Nagoya with one of the defining achievements of Indian Olympic history. At the Paris 2024 Olympics, she won bronze in the women's 10m air pistol and then partnered Sarabjot Singh for another bronze in the 10m air pistol mixed team event — becoming the first athlete from independent India to win two medals at a single edition of the Olympic Games. She also won gold in the women's 25m pistol team event at the Hangzhou 2022 Asian Games, held in 2023.

Her selection continues India's practice of honouring its most bankable medal contenders with the flag: Bhaker will shoot in Nagoya as one of the contingent's strongest podium prospects.

Toor's shot-put dynasty

Toor brings Asian Games pedigree of a different kind. The 31-year-old shot putter won gold in the men's shot put at the 2018 Jakarta Asian Games and defended his title at Hangzhou 2023, making him a two-time defending champion. In Aichi-Nagoya he will attempt to extend that run to three consecutive Asian Games gold medals.

He heads an Indian athletics contingent of more than 70 track and field athletes — including Gulveer Singh, Tejaswin Shankar and Olympian Sarvesh Kushare — that is expected to be a major contributor to India's medal tally.

A record haul to defend

India arrives in Japan aiming to build on a record-breaking performance at Hangzhou 2023, where the contingent finished fourth in the medal standings with 107 medals — 28 gold, 38 silver and 41 bronze. More than 500 Indian athletes are competing across 37 sports in this edition.

The contingent features five individual Olympic medallists despite the withdrawal of defending javelin champion Neeraj Chopra with an ankle injury. PV Sindhu spearheads the badminton campaign, Mirabai Chanu leads the weightlifting team, Aman Sehrawat represents India in wrestling and Lovlina Borgohain in boxing. India will also defend its men's and women's titles in cricket and kabaddi, along with the men's hockey crown. Competition in some sports — including cricket and teqball — began before the opening ceremony.

Diaspora Angle

For the Indian diaspora, the flag-bearers are the familiar face of the contingent: Bhaker's Paris heroics made her a household name in Indian homes worldwide, and her walk into the Nagoya stadium will be one of the most-watched moments of the opening ceremony across diaspora viewing parties.

What's Next

After Saturday's ceremony, the full programme begins in earnest — with shooting, athletics, cricket and hockey among the sports where India has entered as defending champion or strong medal contender, and where the Hangzhou record of 107 medals sets the bar.
